report.answer_text:
Yes—if your local police department or sheriff’s office offers civilian ride-alongs, you can apply to accompany a patrol officer as an observer. You don’t have to be applying for a police job to join a civilian program. (austintexas.gov)
Search your department’s website for “ride-along,” or call its non-emergency number and ask how to apply. Requirements vary: you may need to sign a waiver, meet a minimum age, and apply a few weeks in advance. (austintexas.gov)
What city and state are you in? I can help you find the right application.

context.before:
Ride Along Program
Apply to ride along with an Austin Police officer in the Police Observer (Ride Along) program.
What to know before you apply
Requirements
- Read both the APD Ride Along Policy (586 KB), and
- Read the APD Police Observer program requirements (142 KB).
Things to know
- When selecting your ride date, please keep in mind that it takes 3-4 weeks to get a ride-along scheduled.
-
context.after:
- Riders may only ride ONCE per calendar quarter.
How to submit your form
Once you download and complete your APD Police Observer (Ride Along) form, you can submit it by:
- Emailing APDridealong@austintexas.gov
- In person at APD, 715 East 8th St. Austin, Texas 78701 (APD Public Information Office)
